title: Integer `/`: a division of doubles
verdict: `Int64 / Int64` is `Float64`; `/ 0` is ±inf or NaN; a literal divisor multiplies by its reciprocal
description: `/` on integers casts both operands to `Float64` and divides: `7 / 2` is 3.5, `x / 0` is ±inf, `0 / 0` is NaN. Integers above 2⁵³ round on the way.

The cast happens before the division (binary.rs#L151-L158), so the float kernels run, and a literal or one-row divisor multiplies by its reciprocal (polars-double-scalar-divisor, PL-3): on a frame of two rows or more `49 / 49` is 0.9999999999999999 and `5 / 3` is 1.6666666666666665, and so is `x / x.max()` for `x = 49`.
The docs are silent on the rounding above 2⁵³: a docs gap. The `truediv` docs call the division IEEE 754, which the reciprocal contradicts: PL-8.
No upstream test pins quotients above 2⁵³ or an inexact quotient by a literal; they may change between versions.
reference: Substrait's `divide` on integers returns the integer type and truncates. A plan that divides integers to a double casts first, and the double division's options apply (polars-double-divide).

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

notes: Streaming gives what in memory gives on every probe and observation cited here.
The observations' frames hold a few rows, which streaming runs as one-row morsels; the probes' 6000-row columns cover morsels of many rows.

`python -m sverify_dev.probe_polars --diff --write` runs each probe one row at a time and on a 6000-row column with `collect(engine='in-memory')` and `collect(engine='streaming')`, and each observation twice: its `df(...)` frame's `select`, `with_columns`, `filter`, `sort`, `unique`, `join` and `group_by` go through the streaming engine the second time (`StreamingFrame`); the `s-` observations collect a lazy query on each engine themselves. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.

evidence.note: integer / integer: both cast to Float64, then the float kernel; signed.rs's prim_true_div is not on this route
a length-1 divisor multiplies by its reciprocal

provenance.notes: Corrected the route: an earlier check cited `prim_true_div` of signed.rs, which `Expr /` does not reach. binary.rs#L151-L158 casts both sides to Float64 first, so a literal divisor takes the float reciprocal kernel; added to the description and the verdict.

evidence.note: UInt8 1 / 0 = inf, 0 / 0 = NaN (eager and lazy, both engines; slow)
